requirements.quote:
The simplest form of anti-replay defense is for the server to only
   allow each session ticket to be used once.
requirements.condition: when a server implements the single-use-ticket anti-replay defense
requirements.required_behavior: allow each session ticket to be used at most once
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept a second use of the same session ticket
requirements.why_checkable: The same ticket can be presented twice and successful resumptions or 0-RTT acceptances counted.

requirements.quote:
For instance, the server
   can maintain a database of all outstanding valid tickets, deleting
   each ticket from the database as it is used.  If an unknown ticket is
   provided, the server would then fall back to a full handshake.
requirements.condition: when a server uses the described outstanding-ticket database and receives a ticket absent from that database
requirements.required_behavior: fall back to a full handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: resume the session or accept 0-RTT based on the unknown ticket
requirements.error_behavior: continue with a full handshake rather than accepting the unknown ticket for resumption
requirements.why_checkable: An unrecognized database key can be supplied and the resulting handshake path observed.

requirements.quote:
Unlike session databases,
   session tickets can successfully do PSK-based session establishment
   even without consistent storage, though when 0-RTT is allowed they
   still require consistent storage for anti-replay of 0-RTT data, as
   detailed in the following section.
requirements.condition: when a distributed server deployment allows 0-RTT with session tickets
requirements.required_behavior: use consistent storage sufficient to provide anti-replay protection for the 0-RTT data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: rely on inconsistent ticket storage while claiming the described 0-RTT anti-replay property
requirements.why_checkable: Cross-node replays can test whether ticket-use or ClientHello state is consistently enforced.
